title: Managing API call limits in Airtable
snippet:
[Airtable enforces a rate limit of 5 requests per second](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/rate-limits) (per base) to ensure optimal user performance across all pricing tiers. Additionally, there is a limit of 50 requests per second for all traffic using personal access tokens from a given user or service account. If you exceed this rate, you will receive a 429 status code and must wait 30 seconds before subsequent requests will succeed. API integrations should pause and wait before retrying the API request—behavior handled automatically by the official [JavaScript client](https://github.com/Airtable/airtable.js)—with back-off and retry logic.

# Monthly call limits for Free and Team plans
- Free plan: 1000 API calls per month
- Team plan: 100000 API calls per month
Monthly calls for [Free and Team plans](https://airtable.com/pricing) are also limited to 5 requests per second rate limit.
Detailed API usage analytics are only available for Free plans. Because Team, Business, and Enterprise Scale plans have high or unlimited API call allowances, granular usage tracking is not provided for these plan types.

Airtable's API call limits vary by plan:
- Free: 1,000 API calls per workspace per month. Once exceeded, a 30-day grace period begins.
- Team: 100,000 API calls per workspace per month. Once the limit is reached, API calls are throttled to 2 requests per second.
- Business / Enterprise Scale: No monthly call cap; rate limiting applies per base.

title: Getting started with Airtable's Web API
snippet:
Yes, the Web API has a rate limit of 5 requests per second, per base. This limit is the same across all pricing tiers and increased rate limits are not currently available. For more information, see the "Rate Limits" section of the [API documentation](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/rate-limits).
Are there API call limits?
Yes. These vary by plan type:
- **Free** plan - 1000 calls per workspace per month
- **Team** plan - 100,000 calls per workspace per month
- **Business** and **Enterprise** plans - Unlimited API calls (Still subject to other limits such as the rate limits discussed above)

title: Airtable plans overview
snippet:
The Free plan is intended for individuals or very small teams just getting started with Airtable.

|---|---|

| **Plan features** | - 1000 records per base (1000 records per table max will also hit base record limit) - 1000 [API calls](/docs/getting-started-with-airtables-web-api#api-record-limits) per workspace per month - 1GB per of [attachment storage](/docs/attachment-field) per base - 2 weeks of [revision and snapshot history](/docs/taking-and-restoring-base-snapshots) - 75 unique automations per base - 100 automation runs per workspace per month |

title: Airtable API Pricing 2026: Free vs. Paid Tiers Explained
snippet:
**Airtable API pricing** ties directly to your workspace plan. Each base gets a monthly limit of API calls, and you pay extra if you exceed it. You don’t pay per seat for API access—it’s baked into the plan. But the caps differ dramatically between Free, Plus, Pro, and Enterprise.

Let me explain: on the Free plan, you get 1,200 calls per base per month. That might sound like plenty, but a single integration that syncs 100 records every hour will burn through it in days. The Plus plan bumps you to 5,000 calls, Pro gives 50,000, and Enterprise is custom. Overages kick in after that.

| Plan | Monthly API Calls per Base | Overage Cost (per 1,000 calls) | Key Workspace Additions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 1,200 | Hard cap (no overages) | Up to 1,200 records per base |
| Plus | 5,000 | $1.00 | 5 GB attachments, extensions |
| Pro | 50,000 | $0.50 | Scripting, advanced sync, 20 GB attachments |
| Enterprise | Custom | Negotiable | SSO, admin panel, dedicated support |

The free tier gives you the full API—no feature gaps. You can create, read, update, and delete records, work with attachments, and use all endpoints. The limitation is purely quantitative: 1,200 calls per base per month, plus a per-base record cap of 1,200.
Here’s why that can feel deceptive: if you’re prototyping a tool that syncs daily, 1,200 calls is plenty. But the moment you add a second integration or increase sync frequency, you’ll bust the limit. Many solopreneurs I know design their entire MVP on the Free tier, only to hit the wall right as they get their first users.
Another hidden limitation: the Free plan blocks access to advanced sync features and extensions that help reduce API call count. So you end up writing more custom code, which ironically eats more resources.

Not exactly. Overages are billed automatically on paid plans if you exceed the limit. On Free, there is no option to purchase overage—you must upgrade to Plus or higher. Enterprise customers can negotiate custom pools.

title: Airtable Pricing in 2026: Plans, Per-Seat Math, and the API and Automation Limits That Break Workflows
snippet:
As of October 9, 2026, Airtable costs $0 (Free), $20 per seat a month billed annually on Team ($24 monthly), $45 on Business ($54 monthly), or a custom Enterprise Scale price. Every editor is a paid seat. For automation, Team's real limits are 25,000 automation runs and 100,000 API calls a month per workspace, and one outside tool checking a base every minute uses 43% of that API allowance.

**As of October 9, 2026, Airtable has four plans: Free ($0), Team ($20 per seat a month billed annually, $24 monthly), Business ($45 per seat a month billed annually, $54 monthly) and Enterprise Scale (custom). You pay for every person who can edit at least one base, so a 12-person team where everyone updates records pays $240 a month on Team. For anyone building automations, the plan limits matter more than the seat price: Team caps you at 25,000 automation runs and 100,000 API calls a month per workspace.**

| Plan | Price per seat | Records per base | Automation runs a month | API calls a month | AI credits per seat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 (up to 5 editors) | 1,000 | 100 | 1,000 | 500 |
| Team | $20 billed annually, $24 monthly | 50,000 | 25,000 | 100,000 | 15,000 |
| Business | $45 billed annually, $54 monthly | 125,000 (pricing page card says 100,000) | 100,000 | Unlimited | 20,000 |
| Enterprise Scale | Custom | 500,000 | 500,000 (pricing page card says 1,000,000) | Unlimited | 25,000 |

The Free plan cannot use the "Run a script" automation action, and its "Send email" action can only email people already on the base. Business and Enterprise Scale need a company email domain; Gmail and Yahoo addresses cannot upgrade. Qualifying nonprofits get 50% off the monthly Team price.

- **API calls.** Every request from an outside tool (an automation platform, a custom script or an AI agent reading and writing records) is an API call. Free gets 1,000 a month and Team 100,000, per workspace. Past the Free limit, Airtable gives a one-time 30-day grace period, then blocks calls until the month resets. Past the Team limit, calls slow to 2 requests per second until the 1st.
